---
title: "The CANE format"
guide-section: "Concepts"
description: "What a CANE record is, the four variants, and the grammar."
---

CANE (Context-Anchored Natural Expression) is an output format for named entity recognition
with large language models, introduced in
[*CANE is a Format*](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-emnlp.1398/) (Findings of EMNLP
2026). Instead of character offsets, per-token tags or a marked-up copy of the input, the
model writes one short statement per entity, copied verbatim from the text:

```
Entities:
`metastatic breast cancer` is a DISEASE found in `metastatic breast cancer cells`
`breast cancer cells` is a CELL found in `metastatic breast cancer cells caused`
`headache` and `nausea` are a ADR found in `caused headache and` and `and nausea`
```

Models are good at copying visible text and bad at counting, so CANE never asks for offsets,
token numbers or codes. This library turns those statements back into character spans.

## Records

Each line is a **record**:

- one or more **parts** in backticks: the entity's text, copied verbatim;
- `is a` (or `are a` for several parts) and the **label**, one token;
- optionally `found in` and one **anchor** per part: a short verbatim snippet around the part
  that says *where* in the text it is.

A discontinuous entity, like *headache … nausea* as one adverse reaction, has several parts.

## The four variants

| Variant | Anchor | Discontinuous entities |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| **Base** | ✗ | ✗ |
| **Disco** | ✗ | ✓ |
| **Context** | ✓ | ✗ |
| **Full** | ✓ | ✓ |

The variant is always given explicitly, when writing and when parsing: a line with an anchor
is required in Full but wrong in Base, so the parser must know what the model was asked for.

```{python}
import cane_format as cane

text = "It caused headache and nausea after the first dose."
doc = cane.Document(
    text=text,
    entities=(cane.Entity(spans=[(10, 18), (23, 29)], label="ADR"),),
)
for variant in ("disco", "full"):
    print(f"--- {variant}")
    print(cane.dumps(doc, variant=variant))
```

## Grammar

```
output   ::= HEADER | [HEADER NEWLINE] ( EMPTY | record { NEWLINE record } )
record   ::= [HANDLE] parts COPULA [ARTICLE] LABEL [ANCHOR_INTRO anchors]
parts    ::= QUOTE text QUOTE { PART_CONNECTIVE QUOTE text QUOTE }
anchors  ::= QUOTE text QUOTE { ANCHOR_CONNECTIVE QUOTE text QUOTE }
```

- `NONE`, the header alone, or the header followed by `NONE` mean *no entities*. A completely
  empty output is reported as `empty_output`: it usually means the generation failed.
- There is no escaping. Records are parsed by structure first, so the quote character may
  appear inside a part as long as the record stays unambiguous.
- Whitespace inside parts and anchors matches any run of whitespace in the text.

## Dialects

Every literal (`Entities:`, `NONE`, the backtick, `is` / `are`, `a` / `an`, `found in`,
`and`, the handle prefix `T`) comes from a `Dialect`. The default is `cane.ENGLISH`; another
language or other delimiters are one object away:

```{python}
german = cane.Dialect(
    header="Entitäten:", empty="KEINE", copula_singular="ist", copula_plural="sind",
    articles=("ein", "eine"), anchor_intro="gefunden in", part_connective="und",
    anchor_connective="und",
)
print(cane.dumps(doc, variant="full", dialect=german))
```

Pass the same dialect to `loads` to parse such output.
